channel.title: The Black Hourglass
channel.description: Posts in the discussion thread "The Black Hourglass" - A black hourglass that consumes time itself and a man trying to overcome the guilt he feels for surviving.

item.title: Re: The Black Hourglass
item.content:encoded:
Summoned via PM:

Hi there Dr Hajovsky. Let’s take a look at The Black Hourglass.

+ LBL
- LBL

Item #: SCP-#### The Black Hourglass

Formatting: remember to get rid of “The Black Hourglass” when you post it to the mainlist.

acting site director

Formatting: capitalise all titles.

After initial activation, researcher will be permitted to enter.

Grammar: missing “the” before “researcher”

Time spent within 10 meters of SCP-#### should be kept at an absolute minimum.

This statement is both confusing and vague. Should be reworked so you don’t get mixed up between duration and distance. Also, “absolute minimum” means… what? No longer than 10 minutes? 20 mins? It builds more tension if you included a specific maximum time before the researchers have to leave.

Dr. Licht and SCP-####'s locations are to be monitored at all times.

Isn’t the SCP already confined within the steel cage? Why would its location still need to be monitored then?

Dr. Licht is also not allowed to enter within 10 meters of any personnel

Grammar: you don’t “enter within 10 meters”. Rephrase to “be within” or “approach” or just give him a restraining order.

or civilian unless ordered to do so

This is an interesting condition. So he can approach other people, just that he has to be monitored in some way?

Overall, I’m a little confused by the conprocs, as you spend more time discussing Dr. Licht instead of the actual SCP. You’re setting up some kind of dual narrative here, and I’m intrigued but also worried if you’ll be able to pull off this complexity. Let’s see!

It is 18 cm long and 9 cm at its widest point.

A little glaring that you didn’t include the height.

Its outer layer is comprised of a black, metallic substance of unknown origin.

Similarly, a little glaring you didn’t tell us what its made of internally.

SCP-#### has the ability to create a temporal anomaly capable of consuming the time of macroscopic life within a radius of roughly 10 meters.

Okay, a lot to unpack here. It consumes “time” or “life”? I know you’re hinting at them to be one and the same, but it’s not clear enough. If it kills you, then just say as such, and how.

the length of time the anomaly consumes also appears random.

Grammar: “to be” before “appears”.

Upon activation, SCP-#### will emit several clicks, a loud, low droning sound, and other mechanical noises before quickly expanding and partially exposing the inside of the rectangular prism at its center.

This is detail better suited for your logs later on. I would cut it from the Description, which is meant to be more like an overall log of the scp’s properties.

SCP-#### appears to be designed to permanently bond itself to an humanoid individual, always remaining within a set distance no matter how much force is applied.

This effect came out of nowhere, and I’m not entirely sure why you included it. It’s also not particularly well explained – so the hourglass flies / hovers towards a bonded individual? Or just randomly appears? Need to clarify how this works.

SCP-#### was acquired by the foundation

“Foundation”.

after an anomalous event occurred in the sky above Site-19 on 08-0█-200█

First, there’s no need to tell us “an anomalous event occurred”. Just tell us directly what the anomalous event was. Second, and this is more of personal preference. I wouldn’t redact the year of events. Giving us the year allows the readers to sense where and when this story takes place.

Foundation staff present reported seeing a bright flash of blue light and hearing a loud explosion originating from a point approximately 100 meters above Site-19.

Should have started with this sentence.

While it remains unclear what the exact nature or cause of the anomaly was, it has been designated SCP-####-1.

Huh? Where did this designation come from? Are you referring to the sky event? I would personally cut this as you don’t want to overcomplicate the scp, especially when you’re focused on describing it.

After examining the crash site to make sure it was not biohazardous, Dr. Licht and SCP-#### were escorted by an on site containment team to a standard humanoid containment cell to await examination.

I would think the Foundation’s response would have been more agitated. If something crashed through the roof and suddenly attached itself to a personnel member, security would have quarantined him on the spot, weapons would be trained on the scp etc. This is too muted.

Nine minutes after crashing through the roof of Site-19, SCP-#### and Dr. Licht were being placed into a containment cell.

I don’t think this line is necessary. The information is repeated and redundant. Do we need to know that this specific thing happens after this specific amount of time?

on site containment team

“on-site”.

Contact was never reestablished with the containment team, however, remains with genetic matches to theirs were discovered at [DATA EXPUNGED].

Why is there a redaction here? Weren’t their remains discovered within the containment room?

Dr. Licht was later found in the cell, having suffered no adverse effects.

Okay, so he’s unharmed. But that’s it? What was his reaction? How was he behaving after such a traumatic event?

Addendum ####-02: Recorded Interview-1

The dialogue is generally okay, as is the pacing. What I’m not understanding is this theme of isolation and loneliness arising from Licht, mainly because it wasn’t ever mentioned before. Okay, so some guards died when the thing first arrived. You haven’t mentioned what else happens in between to show Licht’s isolation – does XXXX kill anyone who comes close? Can Licht see his family again? Need to emphasise this a little more before this log.

No tests have yet been conducted with other SCPs that exhibit anomalous corrosive or destructive properties.

Not sure why this line is relevant?

- Testing Documentation

Unsure if intentional, but you need to make this section more readable. Get rid of the mass italics, and use a table or block quotes instead.

Another issue: I don’t see the point of the test-logs. What exactly were you intending to show by this series of tests? To me, the effect seems entirely random: man lives, woman dies, arm disappears, guards disappear as well, man reappears somewhere else. What’s going on? Ideally, you should only include the most pertinent information that serve as variables in the tests. Here, you’re giving us too many details of the test subjects, which I’m assuming don’t actually matter to the results?

Dr. Licht: No, it's fine. I knew I was gonna have to talk about it eventually. [pauses] I was in there for what felt like days

Noting this is repeated info from the earlier audio log. I would cut either this or that.

Addendum ####-08: Containment Breach on 01-1█-0█

Ah? Licht used the object to breach containment? This doesn’t make sense. First, he’s a Foundation researcher. He knows the rules. Second, you haven’t given him a motivation prior to this to do so. Why does he do it? Does he want to visit his family? Has he grown to hate the Foundation because of what they’re doing to him?

Dr. Licht: Still, even if that's the case, I was never given the choice. This was still forced upon me by some cruel act of fate. And now, it feels like I don't have a choice in this either.

Do you see how he logic here doesn’t make sense? How does A=B? Unless the scp is forcing him to be random as well?

+ Overall
- Overall

(+/-) Concept. I’ll be honest: it’s all over the place. The early parts of the article made me think that the anomaly consumed “time” from individuals, thereby taking their lives. But the rest of the article quickly jumped all over the place to spatial displacement, immortality (now I know why you named him “Licht”, and a character arc that doesn’t always make sense.

I get that the focus here is on Licht’s story and how he deals with his newfound powers, but when writing a humanoid entity, you need to give him realistic goals first, and then follow him as he tries to attain them. Here, it seems the scp chose him entirely at random, and what follows are more random events that he gets himself into. If this was intentional btw (i.e., the cube is affecting him and making his actions random / harmful), the connection needs to be spelt out more.

I don’t know, really. You took the story in a different direction from how you set it up, and the payoff wasn’t very strong because the characters and their situations weren’t believable to me.

(+/-) Pacing. The article is too long. Large portions of the Description and Conprocs can be cut / refined to connect better with the rest of the story. I don’t understand what you were going for with the many test-logs – they too need to be refined in terms of direction. I do like the interview logs, though, and the growing relationship between Licht and Lachman. Each log doesn’t overstay its welcome, and the dialogue feels authentic, as are Licht’s emotions in the moment.

Overall, I’m leaning towards a downvote at this point. Reading your original greenlit post now, I would have cautioned you earlier to have linked your themes better. You mention you want a human-driven story of a person dealing with Fate. Okay, but how does that connect to time manipulation and other dimensions? Why does the scp sometimes kill people and at others, transport them through time and space? The link between these two effects needs to be explained better.

If you decide to revise the draft / respond below, do drop me another PM and I’ll take another look. For now, all the best with the writing!

item.title: Re: The Black Hourglass
item.content:encoded:
Thanks for the feedback and suggestions!

+ show block
– hide block

My first main concern is that you didn't cite your image.

The photo is actually something I took and uploaded myself. Would I still need to cite the image or is it fine since it's mine?

The focus of your is on Licht's character arc, but your logs are pretty detached from that. You can also cut down on the description of SCP-####-A through -I by having there only be one button that lets Licht move outside of the flow of time, and then just letting him walk around outside of time instead of using multiple other buttons to do so.

I did want to have some test logs to give the story a bit more time to sink in and develop, as well as flesh out the abilities of the SCP in the reader's minds. However, I do agree that these can be distracting. I attempted to keep them out of the way in collapsibles, but if they are really an issue I can remove them.

I'd put a footnote briefly defining "gravitational lensing", since I imagine most readers won't know what that is.

I didn't really think of that. Nice catch. I'll be sure to add it in the footnotes.

with genetic matches to theirs were discovered at [DATA EXPUNGED]

I don't understand why this is redacted. I'd recommend reading this guide

In my mind, this was redacted to conceal information about the way in which the foundation disposes of staff that die by anomalous means. If it ends up a big issue, I'm open to removing it and writing something in its place.

item.title: Re: The Black Hourglass
item.content:encoded:
+Overall Thoughts
– hide block

Overall, I thought it was alright. You were worried about your dialogue, but it seemed fine to me (however, I'm not the best with dialogue, so you should definitely get a second opinion).

My first main concern is that you didn't cite your image. First, check the image use guidelines and make sure that your image is CC compliant. If it is, put a license box at the bottom of the page. If it isn't, you can't use it in your article. If you want to know where to find CC compliant images, I would recommend Wikimedia Commons and CCSearch.

My second issue are the test logs. The focus of your is on Licht's character arc, but your logs are pretty detached from that. You can also cut down on the description of SCP-####-A through -I by having there only be one button that lets Licht move outside of the flow of time, and then just letting him walk around outside of time instead of using multiple other buttons to do so.

+line-by-line
– hide block

SCP-#### has the ability to create a temporal anomaly capable of consuming the time of macroscopic life

"consuming time" is pretty vague. You explain the effect of this later in the paragraph, but I think you should find a better descriptor for the SCP's effect.

The activation time is inconsistent, along with the amount of time SCP-#### consumes.

I'd change this to "Both the activation time and the amount of time SCP-#### consumes1 are inconsistent."

SCP-#### appears to be designed to permanently attach itself to an humanoid individual. The requirements for this process to occur are as of yet unknown. It is also unknown if it is possible to remove SCP-#### without physically damaging the individual which it has attached to.

This makes it sound like SCP-#### is physically attached to an individual, when the recovery log shows that it just floats near them.

extreme gravitational lensing

I'd put a footnote briefly defining "gravitational lensing", since I imagine most readers won't know what that is (or maybe everyone knows what that is and it's just me).

it has been designated SCP-####-2

I'd change it to SCP-####-1 since you never mentioned -1.

with genetic matches to theirs were discovered at [DATA EXPUNGED]

I don't understand why this is redacted. I'd recommend reading this guide

I just happen to be in the wrong place

You don't need to change this since dialogue doesn't have to have perfect grammar, but "happen" should be "happened"

Subject entered within 10 meters of SCP-####. Immediately, SCP-#### began activating, and subject disappeared from the cell.

I'd change this to "SCP-#### activated immediately after subject entered within 10 meters of SCP-####." You can remove "subject disappeared from the cell" because the next couple sentences imply that the subject disappeared.

Subject 6 was found to have transported to a closed doorway, and suffered [DATA EXPUNGED]. Subject died █ minutes after initial recovery.

I'd change this to "Subject 6 was found to have been transported inside of a closed doorway and could not be recovered." Saying that they couldn't be recovered implies that they were located but died before they could be properly rescued.

item.title: The Black Hourglass - SCP
item.content:encoded:
Hi there. This is my first SCP draft so here is the link to my greenlights: Idea Thread

I've made some major changes per the suggestions made in that thread and would like your feedback. Some things I'm looking for critique on include: clinical tone, line by line, general formatting, and emotional impact, although critique of any kind is appreciated. I also think that dialogue is one of my weaker points as a writer, so I'm definitely looking for opinions on that.

Here's the link to my sandbox: http://scp-sandbox-3.wikidot.com/dr-hajovsky
